tool: Hunspell 1.7.2 library, stem() and spell() (hstem.cpp), LibreOffice dictionaries at commit c0865a85
paradigms: scripts/language/check/declension.py (singular, by the word's ending; written by hand, not fetched)
rule: Which candidate forms of a name word stand. A form is dropped when Hunspell knows it as an ordinary word: in Russian and Polish, where a dictionary writes its proper nouns with a capital, when it accepts the form in lower case (Банки, "banks"; Kora, "bark"), unless every entry it is a form of is the name itself; in German and Arabic, when it accepts the form as a form of anything but the name. An entry made from the name (Polish «achillesowy», the adjective of Achilles) is the name's; in Arabic so is any entry Hunspell gives for the name alone (`own`), because its dictionary parses an unknown name too (روميو as رومي and و), and the prefix then adds nothing. A form that is also another proper noun (Russian «Афины», Athens and Athena's genitive) is kept and listed as a homograph.
use: build_card_text.py writes the forms that stand into the card text (pack.forms); src/lib/verse/echo.ts counts a verse word as a name when it is the name or one of them
